tagline: A quiet island at the far edge of Trat — Khlong Chao waterfall, white sand and clear water, a giant makha tree, and old fishing villages
introHtml:
Koh Kood is the last big island off Thailand's eastern coast, in Trat province right by the Cambodian border. It's still quiet and the nature is intact — clear water, white sand, and no main road or convenience stores like you'd find on busier islands. People come to Koh Kood to slow down and skip the crowds.

The highlights are Khlong Chao waterfall, which is big and pretty, the quieter Khlong Yai Ki waterfall, Ao Tapao and Ao Phrao beaches with clear water and white sand, the fishing villages at Khlong Chao and Ao Salad where the old sea-village way of life lives on, and a giant makha tree several hundred years old. If you love the sea, you can take a boat out to snorkel at Koh Rang. · honesty: getting to Koh Kood takes a while, and many places close during the May–Oct monsoon. Things cost more on the island because everything has to be shipped in, and phone signal and power can be limited in spots — check with your accommodation first.
bestTime: November–April brings clear water and calm seas, great for swimming and snorkeling — this is high season when the island is fully open · May–October is monsoon, with rough seas and many resorts and boat operators shut

highlights.name: Khlong Chao Waterfall
highlights.blurb: The biggest and best-known waterfall on Koh Kood, with a wide pool to swim in and cool, clear water in the middle of the forest. A former royal visiting spot and a popular place to cool off.

highlights.name: Ao Tapao Beach
highlights.blurb: A long white-sand beach with clear water on the island's west side. Quiet, with lovely sunsets, and home to resorts and beachside restaurants.

highlights.name: Ao Phrao Beach
highlights.blurb: A white-sand beach with shallow, clear water that's good for swimming and lazing around. Calm and quiet, with resorts and a sunset view over the sea.

highlights.name: Giant Makha Tree
highlights.blurb: A huge makha-mong tree several hundred years old deep in Koh Kood's forest. The trunk is wide enough to need several people to wrap around it — a quick nature and photo stop.

highlights.name: Ao Salad Fishing Village
highlights.blurb: An old fishing village on the island's north end where the sea-village way of life carries on — wooden houses over the water, seafood spots, and a fishing pier. Simple and easygoing.

highlights.name: Snorkeling at Koh Rang
highlights.blurb: Take a boat out to snorkel at Koh Rang, where the water is clear and the coral is healthy. A popular sea trip from Koh Kood on calm days.

foodScene.name: Fresh seafood
foodScene.note: Koh Kood is a fishing island, with fresh seafood at the Khlong Chao and Ao Salad villages — shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish cooked fresh, and cheaper than at the resorts.

foodScene.name: Beach bars and restaurants
foodScene.note: Ao Tapao and Ao Phrao have beachside restaurants and bars where you can eat, drink, and watch the sunset in a relaxed, quiet-island mood.

foodScene.name: Small cafes
foodScene.note: The island has little cafes serving fresh coffee and desserts dotted along the beaches and villages — a good place to pause for a coffee during the day.

foodScene.name: Local and made-to-order food
foodScene.note: The villages have made-to-order and local eateries at local prices — bold flavors and good value, a cheaper option than the resort restaurants.

attractions.name: Khlong Chao Waterfall
attractions.blurb: The biggest and best-known waterfall on Koh Kood, with a wide pool you can swim in and cool, clear water in the forest. A former royal visiting spot and a popular place to cool off.

attractions.name: Khlong Yai Ki Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tiered waterfall that's quieter than Khlong Chao, with clear pools and a short forest trail — good for nature lovers who want to skip the crowds.

attractions.name: Ao Tapao Beach
attractions.blurb: A long white-sand beach with clear water on the west side. Quiet, with lovely sunsets, plus resorts and beachside restaurants.

attractions.name: Ao Phrao Beach
attractions.blurb: A white-sand beach with shallow, clear water that's good for swimming and relaxing. Calm and quiet, with a sunset view over the sea.

attractions.name: Bang Bao Beach
attractions.blurb: A small, quiet beach and bay on Koh Kood with clear water for swimming, beachside places to stay, and a private feel.

attractions.name: Giant Makha Tree
attractions.blurb: A huge makha-mong tree several hundred years old in the forest, the trunk wide enough to need several people to wrap around it — a nature and photo stop.

attractions.name: Ao Salad Fishing Village
attractions.blurb: An old fishing village where the sea-village way of life carries on — wooden houses over the water, seafood spots, and a pier. Simple and easygoing.

attractions.name: Snorkeling at Koh Rang
attractions.blurb: Take a boat out to snorkel at Koh Rang, with clear water and healthy coral — a popular sea trip on calm days.
